output.brief:
The fall in first-contact resolution is most likely caused by Finance's credit-handling change FC-0417, live on 14 April. It cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25, so billing calls that agents used to settle now get referred to the Billing Resolution team. Referrals jumped from 7% to 54% in the same week, and referred calls resolve only about a third of the time. Calls that were not referred still resolve at 82%, the same as before. The new agents are not the cause: tenured agents show the same drop, and the April intake is referred at the same rate. The IVR change came after the drop began, and tariff calls resolve as well as before.

Confidence is reasonable but not certain. The timing and mechanism are strong. The causal link is inferred, not tested. Do not put the April intake on performance plans. Run Action A1: a limited trial of a revised in-call credit authority with post-call sampling, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Also ask Finance to explain why Customer Operations was not consulted.
